title: Hybrid ephemeral reserve and latency-aware admission controller for embeddings
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We observe frequent short-duration spikes from a small subset of tenants that blow past provisioned capacity and cause p99 latency regressions for embeddings endpoints. Current autoscalers are reactive and slow to capture micro-bursts; the queuing layer either allows long tail delays or drops into global backpressure, hurting high-priority customers.

Goal: Implement a hybrid runtime admission controller that uses: 1) a small pool of ephemeral reserve slots (pre-warmed containers/VM-backed workers) to absorb micro-bursts, and 2) a latency-aware admission policy that dynamically adjusts per-tenant token-buckets and batch sizing to keep p95/p99 under SLOs while preserving overall throughput and unit cost. The system should allow soft reservations for tenants with burst budgets, hard-fallback to fair-drop policies when reserves exhausted, and observability to tie regressions to tenant signals.

Scope: prototype admission controller + ephemeral pool allocator for embeddings-only fleet, integration with existing request router and metrics, and a 2-week canary in a low-latency region.

Non-goals: Embeddings model sharding, long-lived dedicated pool re-architecture, or cross-service rate shaping for other endpoints (chat/generation) in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for embeddings across canary tenants <= 45ms and p99 <= 150ms under 3x baseline burst (validated via synthetic load)
Successful absorption of 90% of synthetic 5s micro-bursts without triggering global autoscale events
Dashboard shows per-tenant burst budget usage and ephemeral pool utilization
No >1% increase in token-cost per 100k tokens for steady-state traffic during canary
Playbook entries for debugging admission decisions and manual reserve adjustments exist in Confluence
engineering_notes: Admission controller responsibilities: evaluate tenant burst budget, current queue depth, model inference latency estimates, and ephemeral pool headroom. Return admit/queue/drop decisions with priority tags.

Ephemeral pool: keep N lightweight workers per AZ (configurable), pre-warm with KV cache disabled but quick model load; warm-up time targeted <800ms. Pool scales independently of main autoscaler based on observed micro-burst frequency metric (burst_events/min).
Token-bucket per tenant: two-band bucket (steady-state refill r_s, burst refill r_b). Implement soft borrowing from burst band with graceful exhaustion (backoff signals to client).

Batch sizing: controller suggests max batch size per request based on current estimated tail risk. For very short bursts, reduce batch size to preserve p99 at cost of throughput. Employ a small quantized set of batch sizes to simplify kernel selection.

Fallback: when ephemeral pool and burst tokens exhausted, mark tenant requests as LOW_PRIORITY and apply best-effort batching; if queue depth crosses threshold, start soft-dropping requests from lowest-priority tenants with early 429/503 hints and guidance header for retry-after.
Metrics to emit: admit_rate_by_tenant, burst_budget_remaining, ephemeral_pool_fill, burst_events_per_min, queue_wait_time_distribution, p95/p99_by_tenant, cost_per_token_delta

Tradeoffs: adding ephemeral pool increases baseline resource footprint and slightly higher idle costs; however it reduces frequency of expensive scale-outs. Quantized batch sizes may reduce kernel-optimality for some sequences but simplify latency predictions.
Security: ephemeral workers must obey tenant isolation and audit logs; ensure KMS access patterns unchanged. No persistent tenant data retained by ephemeral nodes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): standalone simulator that replays production traces and validates admission decisions (2d)
Phase 1 (staging): deploy admission controller and ephemeral pool in staging; run synthetic micro-burst tests vs control cluster (3d)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% traffic of low-risk tenants in us-west-2 for 2 weeks; monitor SLOs and cost delta
Phase 3 (ramp): expand to 30% then 70% with automated rollback if p99 or error-rate increases > 3x
Phase 4 (GA): enable config and tenant opt-in via Console; documentation and runbook published
monitoring_and_alerts: SLO alert: p99 embeddings > 150ms for canary group for 5m -> Pager
Utilization alert: ephemeral_pool_fill > 90% for 2m -> Pager + auto-increase ephemeral target by 1
Burst budget anomaly: >3x expected burst_events/min for 10m -> Investigate tenant pattern
Cost anomaly: token-cost-per-100k tokens delta > 5% sustained for 30m -> Slack ops-alert
